title: Chicken Tikka Masala
shortDescription: Rich curry on a busy night
subtitle: Rich curry on a busy night
description: Rich curry on a busy night. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Chicken Tikka Masala in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate chicken
steps.instruction: Coat cubed chicken thighs in tikka marinade; rest at least 30 minutes. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Char the chicken
steps.instruction: Broil or grill marinated chicken on racks until edges char and centers reach 165°F. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the masala
steps.instruction: Sweat diced onion in oil 8 minutes. Add crushed tomatoes and cream; simmer 15 minutes. Fold in charred chicken; simmer 10 minutes more. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Chicken Tikka Masala onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve with basmati
steps.instruction: Fluff basmati rice. Ladle tikka masala over rice with naan on the side if you have it. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Tikka Masala with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Chicken Tikka Masala on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Rich curry on a busy night. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
